newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers to offer bill on Internet taxes.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers to offer bill on Internet taxes.

text.p: A Senator and a House lawmaker plan Thursday to introduce legislation that would keep the Internet free of state and local sales taxes as well as taxes for hooking up to the global computer network.

The bill, to be offered by Senator Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) and Representative Chris Cox (R-Calif.) also will call on the Clinton administration to develop a comprehensive plan to address the issue of electronic commerce taxes, the lawmakers said Wednesday.

Cox's office said the bill is "aimed at ensuring the continued technological development of the Internet by protecting both Internet users and electronic commerce conducted over the Internet from burdensome state and local taxes and foreign tariffs."
Last November, the Clinton administration said that no special taxes should be imposed in cyberspace.
It also said in a report that the Treasury Department is not considering any new type of value added tax, 'bit' tax, or other new excise tax on electronic commerce.
Businesses, meanwhile, are strugging with a variety of tax proposals from state and local governments that would affect cyberspace.
